Elena —

Appreciate the checklist. I filled this out inline below to make review quicker. Short summary up front: Redwood Hosted API keeps customer inference payloads ephemeral by default; persistent storage is limited to metrics/operational logs (configurable). For EU customers we prefer regional handling and can scope backups/retention to EU-only infrastructure under our EU region. Full answers: 

1) Request/response logs:
- By default: transient in-memory streaming with short-lived KV caches. No persistent transcript storage unless customer enables logging.
- Optional request logs: if enabled, they are stored in the customer region (EU region: eu-central-1) and retained per tenant policy. Default retention when enabled: 30 days.

2) Backup snapshots:
- We take configuration and state snapshots for service continuity. Model artifacts are immutable and stored in our model catalog (not customer PII).
- Backups that could include cached metadata are stored in the EU region for EU-scoped tenants and retained for 30 days before automated deletion. For longer retention customers we provide a contract amendment.

3) Deletion / Erasure procedure:
- Customer-initiated erasure (API or ticket): we queue a tenant purge job that removes all tenant-specific logs, cached prefixes, and KV entries. SLA: 72 hours for full purge from active systems, and 30 days to remove from backup snapshots.
- We provide a purge report (machine-readable) after completion containing purge timestamps and object IDs.

4) Metadata retention:
- Minimal operational metadata (non-identifying telemetry, usage counters) is stored for diagnostics and aggregated reporting. Default window: 90 days.
- Tenant identifiers (tenant_id, region tag) may remain in aggregation until retention expiry but payloads/fields are not preserved.

5) Audit & evidence:
- We maintain audit logs for purge operations and administrative access for 12 months (EU region). Audits include operator id, timestamp, and object IDs affected.

6) Snapshots & restore:
- Restores are operationally gated; to restore tenant data we require a signed request from an authorized admin and we log the restore event to the audit trail.

7) Additional controls:
- KMS integration: keys can be customer-managed in EU (bring-your-own-key).
- HSM-backed key splits available for enterprise private deploys (discussed post-contract).

I attached a lightweight data flow diagram showing EU-only routing and the purge job flow. If you want formal language for your questionnaire, Ben drafted a one-page response we can drop into your template — cc’ing him.

Attachment: [redwood_data_flow_diagram_v3.png]

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

--- Inline answers (as they map to BH questionnaire fields) ---
Q1. Where do you persist request/response data?
A1: Not persisted by default. Optional logging stored in EU region (eu-central-1) when enabled. Default retention 30 days.

Q2. How long are backups kept?
A2: Operational snapshots kept up to 30 days for EU-scoped tenants; removal scheduled automatically. For contractual longer retention, we offer options.

Q3. How is deletion verified?
A3: Tenant purge job + verification pass; machine-readable purge report and audit record. SLA 72h active purge; 30d backup expiry.

Q4. Any residual metadata?
A4: Aggregated telemetry retained 90d; tenant_id and non-sensitive counters can persist until expiry but payloads removed.

Q5. Can keys be customer-managed?
A5: Yes, KMS BYOK in EU supported.

Elena — quick answers to those legal points below; I'm Kimberly (Legal Ops) and handle the contractual wording. Ben and I coordinated on the language.

1) Immutable snapshots / cold archival:
- Our standard hosting plan does not place tenant-specific payloads into long-term immutable archives. Backups are operational snapshots kept for up to 30 days and rotated; they are not copied to a separate immutable cold archive for tenants by default.
- In rare disaster scenarios we may ship a forensics snapshot to secure, access-controlled storage; such snapshots are retained only as long as necessary for recovery and are treated as containing the same removal constraints. We document any such event and include it in the purge report.

2) Early removal from backups/archives: 
- Yes. For compliance-driven erasure requests, we initiate an expedited backup purge workflow that attempts to remove the tenant from backups where feasible. Because of distributed replication, the operational target for expedited backup purge is 14 days. We will provide a certificate of removal indicating when the expedited purge completed.

3) Suggested text for your questionnaire (paste-ready):

"Redwood Inference (Hosted API) processes inference requests in-memory by default and does not persist request/response payloads unless logging is explicitly enabled by the customer. Where enabled, logs and operational snapshots are stored in the customer's chosen region (EU: eu-central-1) and retained for 30 days. Customer-initiated erasure triggers a tenant purge that removes tenant-specific logs, caches, and metadata from active systems within 72 hours; removal from backups is completed within 30 days under our standard process or within 14 days under an expedited compliance purge. A machine-readable purge report and audit record will be provided on completion."

If you want this in your questionnaire PDF we can send a signed short attestation.
